strengths: Novel self-alignment framework leveraging internal consistency of meta-predictions as reward signal, eliminating need for external supervision
Comprehensive empirical validation across six mathematical benchmarks and three model sizes with extensive ablation studies
Convincing analysis of training dynamics (Figure 3) demonstrating meta-awareness directly drives performance more than training steps alone
Practical training efficiency improvements of 1.28× speedup demonstrated via MAPR-efficient variant
Cross-algorithm generalization validated on both GRPO and DAPO; out-of-domain testing on logical, scientific, and coding tasks
Code and detailed implementation provided in appendices for reproducibility; standard deviations reported across experimental runs
weaknesses: Reward function design choices lack principled justification: exponential decay base (0.01) for difficulty reward appears arbitrary despite ablations; notion reward is overly simplistic (binary indicator), discarding correlation strength information

Notion component impact inconsistent: Table 5 shows negligible improvement from notion feedin (MAPR+NF ≈ MAPR), contradicting Shapley analysis (67.1% contribution in Figure 6a); GRPO+NF requires impractical cross-model notion extraction

Out-of-domain generalization limited: Table 8 shows modest 1-2% improvements on logical/scientific/coding tasks without domain-specific training, raising questions about generality of meta-awareness framework

Methodological concern in Figure 3a: paired analysis conflates training iterations with meta-awareness improvement; causal claim that 'meta-awareness drives performance more than training' needs stronger justification
Static online gating design suboptimal: previously gated tasks never revisited despite potential model improvement; dynamic re-evaluation dismissed as costly without quantitative justification
Computational overhead not fully accounted: meta-predictions add 15.5% token cost; efficiency gains in MAPR-efficient come largely from gating/cutoff orthogonal to core meta-alignment mechanism
Notion extraction methodology underdescribed: 'lemma-based matching' not formally defined; unclear how this would generalize beyond mathematics or be implemented independently
Statistical significance testing absent: many improvements fall within 1-2 standard deviations; absolute performance on hardest benchmarks remains low (AIME'25: 21.56% on 4B)

Failure case analysis missing: performance actually degrades on Minerva (4B: -3.18%), Llama 3.1 Olympiad and Gemma 2 tasks with minimal explanation; hyperparameter k=80 chosen in data-driven manner with unclear generalization
Reward normalization: equal weighting of three components with different ranges (Eq. 2) not justified; moving target ground truth for length reward could cause training instability

strengths: Well-motivated approach using self-generated predictions as alignment-based rewards for meta-awareness without external supervision
Rigorous experimental methodology with comprehensive evaluation across 6 benchmarks, multiple model sizes, and thorough ablation studies
Strong empirical results, particularly on harder benchmarks (AIME25: +83.18%, AIME24: +49.43%) and practical training efficiency gains (1.28× speedup)
Insightful training dynamics analysis revealing 'drop-then-align' phenomenon correlating prediction calibration with performance gains
Demonstrates generalization across model families (Llama, Gemma, Qwen) and RL algorithms (GRPO, DAPO) with only 15.5% computational overhead
Strong reproducibility with provided code snippets, complete hyperparameters, implementation details, and statistical reporting
Clever paired analysis (Figure 3a) isolating meta-awareness impact from training duration, showing performance more sensitive to meta-awareness than training steps
weaknesses: Reward design lacks strong theoretical justification: length reward uses coarse binary indicator, difficulty reward uses arbitrary exponential decay without ablation, and notion reward contributes only 8.4% of performance gains
Performance improvements diminish substantially with model scale (13.04% at 4B → 6.63% at 14B) and are minimal on easier benchmarks, but lack analysis of underlying causes or practical implications
Causality not definitively established: Figure 3a shows correlation between meta-awareness and performance but cannot rule out that both are consequences of better model learning
Predictive gating threshold selection (σ_pg) appears empirically driven without principled justification or discussion of generalization to different datasets/domains
Notion component methodology underspecified ('lemma-based matching') with minimal empirical validation; MAPR+NF provides little benefit over MAPR (Table 5) despite expectations
Contribution is somewhat incremental as an auxiliary loss added to existing GRPO/DAPO; individual components (difficulty assessment, length constraints) not novel
Asymmetry in notion feedin analysis: MAPR+NF provides minimal gain for MAPR model but significant gain for independently trained GRPO, suggesting overfitting but lacks investigation
Out-of-domain generalization is modest (1-2% improvements on logical/scientific/coding tasks), suggesting meta-awareness learned is domain-specific to mathematics

Design choices rely on heuristics: exponential decay form chosen without alternatives tested, pass rate discretized to 0-8 without empirical justification, reward components averaged equally without learned weighting
